title: A USD payment settled to a Swedish merchant at a 1:1 rate
details:
Treasury escalated this one and it is the most expensive thing on this list.

A merchant settling in SEK was paid out for USD 100.00 and received SEK 100.00. The mid-market rate that
day was around 10.4, so they were underpaid by roughly a factor of ten. Three merchants are affected and
the total exposure is a little over USD 40,000.

The treasury feed had not published a USD/SEK rate that morning — the corridor was added last week and
the feed configuration had not been updated. That is our operational mistake and we have fixed the feed.

What we cannot live with is what the system did about it. With no rate available, the conversion returned
the same number in the target currency and the payout went out as if nothing were wrong. There is no
error in the logs, no alert, and nothing on the settlement report to show the amount was never actually
converted.

A conversion we cannot price has to fail loudly so the payout is held. Silently substituting a rate — any
rate — is not an acceptable outcome. Corridors that DO have a published rate must keep working exactly as
they do now, including the inverse of a quoted pair.
